def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S Fm] (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓢]
    (K F : Fm → Fm) (conF φ : Fm),
    Def10 𝓢 K →
    𝓢 ⊢ K (conF 🡒 F φ 🡒 φ) →
    𝓢 ⊢ F φ 🡒 K (F φ) →
    𝓢 ⊢ ∼K φ ⋏ F φ 🡒 ∼K conF
translation: Target asserts the following proposition: For all types Fm (of sentences) and S (of proof systems), any choice of formal logical connectives (implication 🡒, conjunction ⋏, disjunction ⋎, negation ∼, truth ⊤, and falsehood ⊥) on Fm, any provability relation ⊢ between S and Fm, any proof system 𝓢 in S that proves every classical propositional tautology in these connectives and is closed under modus ponens, any functions K and F from Fm to Fm, and any sentences conF and φ in Fm: if (1) for all sentences α and β in Fm, 𝓢 proves K (α 🡒 β) 🡒 (K α 🡒 K β), (2) 𝓢 proves K (conF 🡒 (F φ 🡒 φ)), and (3) 𝓢 proves F φ 🡒 K (F φ), then 𝓢 proves ((∼(K φ)) ⋏ (F φ)) 🡒 ∼(K conF). Nothing else is assumed: 𝓢 is not required to be consistent or closed under any additional rules (such as necessitation for K or F); K and F are arbitrary functions from Fm to Fm with no further properties required; and conF is simply an arbitrary sentence in Fm with no requirement relating it to F or to consistency beyond its appearance in hypothesis (2) and the conclusion.

divergences.description: Quantifier elimination and omission of line (∗∗): the source derives the corollary from K(ConsF → (∀ϕ ∈ L(PA))(Fϕ → ϕ)), which requires moving the bounded universal quantifier outside K using line (∗∗) (ϕ ∈ L(PA) → K(ϕ ∈ L(PA))) and a quantifier-modality step (elided in the source's '[…]'). The TARGET instantiates the K-intro line inside K at a single sentence φ—namely K(conF 🡒 F φ 🡒 φ)—omitting the quantifiers, membership in L(PA), line (∗∗), and the quantifier-K interaction step. This is explicitly declared by the author as a single-sentence idealization.

Upstream derivations entered as hypotheses: the source proves line (∗) (Fϕ → K(Fϕ)) from Σ1-completeness and the Rule of mathematical knowledge, and proves the K-intro line from 'Cons implies Sound', determinateness, and the K-intro rule. The TARGET omits those upstream derivations and takes both lines as hypotheses, formalizing only the downstream classical-epistemic deduction to the corollary (as stated in the claim).

Abstract idealization of the system and predicates: 𝓢 is an arbitrary classical propositional system and K, F, conF, φ are arbitrary functions and sentences, with no modelling of arithmetic, Gödel coding, the specific system DTK, or the relationship between conF and F. This is a harmless strengthening/idealization relative to the propositional core of the proof.

Object-level implication vs. derivability from a premise: the source states the corollary as (∃ϕ ∈ L(PA))(¬Kϕ ∧ Fϕ) ⊢DTK ¬K(ConsF), whereas the TARGET concludes with an internal conditional theorem 𝓢 ⊢ ∼K φ ⋏ F φ 🡒 ∼K conF. Under classical logic this is a harmless presentational choice (and yields the premise-to-conclusion derivability by modus ponens).

judgement.summary: As a single-sentence abstract rendering of the downstream proof of the corollary, the TARGET is faithful: its three hypotheses match Distributivity of K, the single-sentence instantiation of the K-intro line, and line (∗), and its conclusion matches the single-sentence form of the corollary. The divergences are minor and largely declared: the Lean omits arithmetic, coding, quantifiers, line (∗∗), the quantifier-K step, and the upstream derivations of (∗) and the K-intro line.
